messages:
incident-bot: Paging @sara_oncall (on-call infra) for SEV-2: multiple serving runtime pods showing NCCL timeouts and hangs on tensor-parallel jobs. Alert rate: 12 errors/min. Impact: ~30% inference failures on /generate for customers in us-west1. Please ack.

sara_oncall: acked. I'm online. Initial glance?

mike_infra: seeing repeated NCCL WARN and timeout messages in the pod logs across 3 nodes: 
```
2024-08-05T03:20:10Z runtime-container[pid]: NCCL WARN Call to cudaMemcpy stalled for > 10s
2024-08-05T03:20:10Z runtime-container[pid]: NCCL WARN connection timed out with rank 2
2024-08-05T03:21:02Z runtime-container[pid]: cudaGetLastError() -> CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS
```

alex_runtime: confirmed. Topology: pipeline parallel with 4 GPUs across 2 hosts. The communicator appears to deadlock during a large attention pass. CPU mem okay, GPU memory sometimes spikes then OOM on rank 2.

sara_oncall: mike, can you isolate which nodes/pods are affected?

mike_infra: affected pods: runtime-pp-7d6c9 (node:gpu-a-03), runtime-pp-7d6c9-1 (node:gpu-a-04), runtime-pp-7d6c9-2 (node:gpu-b-01). All in ns=redwood-serving.

jen_cs: customers: two major PLG customers hitting increased latency and error 500s. CS will open a customer-facing update once we have mitigation.

alex_runtime: immediate mitigations I propose: 1) scale-down to single-GPU model variant for impacted routes (fallback model) 2) set NCCL_TIMEOUT=600000 env for new pods 3) restart the hung pods to break the communicator 4) drain node gpu-b-01 if kernel driver looks unstable. Which to try first?

sara_oncall: runband: do the least-impactful first. Can we shift traffic to a compatible single-GPU variant?

alex_runtime: yes, we have a compatible quantized variant (redwood/opt-lite-1g) that can serve same API with slightly higher latency but avoids multi-GPU collectives. I can flip routing rule in 2-3 mins.

mike_infra: I'm going to cordon gpu-b-01 and restart the runtime pods there. Doing `kubectl cordon gpu-b-01` then `kubectl delete pod runtime-pp-7d6c9-2 -n redwood-serving` to force reschedule.

incident-bot: @sara_oncall acknowledged the incident at 2024-08-05T03:21:14Z.

sara_oncall: alex, please flip routing for the affected route to the single-GPU variant now. I'll restart pods on gpu-b-01 after mike deletes the pod.

alex_runtime: flipping routing rule: `POST /admin/routing/overrides` with body `{ "route": "/generate", "model": "redwood/opt-lite-1g", "reason": "mitigate NCCL multi-gpu hang" }` -> 200 OK.

jen_cs: noted. I'll draft a short message: "We're routing a subset of traffic to a single-GPU fallback to reduce errors and latency spikes; no data loss expected; working on restoring full capacity."

mike_infra: pod runtime-pp-7d6c9-2 deleted, node logs show NVML driver reset around the time of the hang. Running a quick health check.

alex_runtime: adding to mitigation: increase NCCL debug/env on new pods so we can gather traces if recreates: set NCCL_DEBUG=INFO NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING=1 NCCL_ALGO=RING for now. We'll also reduce max_batch_tokens to 512 to avoid large collective IO.

sara_oncall: good. After routing flip and pod restart, are error rates dropping?

mike_infra: deploying: restarted pods on gpu-b-01 and gpu-a-04. Watching logs...

mike_infra: error rate initial drop to 7 errors/min, then 2 errors/min after 4 minutes. Latency for /generate increased ~120ms on fallback variant but success rate improved to 98%.

alex_runtime: capturing logs for all ranks and fetching backtraces. Command used: 
```
kubectl logs runtime-pp-7d6c9 -n redwood-serving -c runtime --since=10m > /tmp/pp-rank0.log
for pod in runtime-pp-*; do kubectl exec -n redwood-serving $pod -c runtime -- gdb -q -ex 'thread apply all bt' -ex 'quit' --batch > /tmp/$pod.bt || true; done
```

jen_cs: forwarded status to customers: "We've applied a routing mitigation and are restoring normal service; we'll follow up with engineering root cause." Customers acknowledged.

oliver_pm: any known recent changes that could've triggered this? kernel/driver upgrades or model rollout?

mike_infra: no kernel or driver pushes in last 24h. There was a model rollout 2h ago but to a small percentage. I'm reverting rollout to be safe.

alex_runtime: rollback of the small model rollout confirmed. The rollout increased batch window; probably pushed collectives into less frequent but larger calls. Could have exposed a race in communicator init. We'll mark that as likely.

sara_oncall: good. Next steps: 1) keep fallback routing for 1 hour while we re-create pods with NCCL envs and smaller batch size 2) run a controlled canary of multi-gpu variant with heavy watchdog/timeout 3) prepare node-level diagnostics and escalate to driver vendor if NVML resets persist.

mike_infra: will keep gpu-b-01 cordoned for 30m and run stress memtest on gpu-a-03/04. I'll also collect dmesg + nvidia-smi -q outputs.

alex_runtime: will prepare a deterministic repro using the same pipeline config and run in our staging cluster with NCCL_DEBUG=TRACE to hit the failure. Also will add stronger per-request timeouts to avoid cascading waits.

jen_cs: customers are ok with temporary performance hit; they asked for ETA on full multi-GPU restore. Can we commit to a rough timeline?

sara_oncall: aiming for 2-4 hours for full restore depending on repro. I'll update CS in 30m.

incident-bot: Incident SEV-2 - mitigation in place. Current status: partial degraded -> majority routed to single-GPU fallback. Errors reduced to baseline.

sara_oncall: wrapping up handoff to night on-call @mike_infra at 2024-08-05T04:05:05Z. Mike, you're primary now for follow-ups and RCA.

mike_infra: acknowledged handoff. I'll keep monitoring and post final notes once node checks complete.

alex_runtime: summary for RCA: probable cause - larger batch windows from recent rollout causing NCCL collectives to hit a race/timeout on multi-host communicator; observed NVML GPU resets on one host causing rank communicator failure and subsequent hang. Mitigations applied: routing fallback, pod restarts, node cordon, increased NCCL_TIMEOUT and logging, rollback of rollout, reduced batch sizes. Next: reproduce in staging, add guardrails to rollout pipeline to limit collective sizes, and add automated fallback policy when NCCL errors spike.

jen_cs: thanks all. I'll keep customers updated with the summary and ETA.

incident-bot: Incident resolved when mitigation achieved at 2024-08-05T04:11:45Z (status: monitoring).
